body.en: *Vital statistics* is the branch of statistics that deals with vital events of human life: births, deaths, marriages, divorces and migration. Population statistics studies the size, composition and growth of a population using these events. Vital rates are expressed per 1000 of the mid-year population, for example $\text{Rate} = \frac{\text{events}}{P} \times 1000$.

explanation.en: The census counts everyone at one time, once in ten years. Registration records births, deaths and marriages continuously as they happen, as the law requires. Sample surveys such as the Sample Registration System estimate rates where registration is incomplete.

body.en: Census method: a complete count of the population at one time; in India it is taken every 10 years. Registration method: births and deaths are registered continuously as they occur (Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969). Survey (sample) method: special surveys such as the Sample Registration System give estimates where registration is incomplete. Uses: planning health, education and housing; comparing the health of regions; fixing insurance premiums; studying population growth.

problem.en: The population of a town was 2,40,000 on 1 January and 2,60,000 on 31 December. There were 6,000 births and 2,250 deaths during the year. Find the crude birth rate, crude death rate and natural growth rate.

steps.en: Natural growth rate = CBR − CDR = 24 − 9 = 15 per thousand (1.5%).

narration.en: Let us work this out together. The population of a town was 2,40,000 on 1 January and 2,60,000 on 31 December. There were 6,000 births and 2,250 deaths during the year. Find the crude birth rate, crude death rate and natural growth rate.

say.en: Let us work this out together. The population of a town was 2,40,000 on 1 January and 2,60,000 on 31 December. There were 6,000 births and 2,250 deaths during the year. Find the crude birth rate, crude death rate and natural growth rate.
Mid-year population is approximately (2,40,000 plus 2,60,000)/2 equals 2,50,000.
CBR equals 6,000 over 2,50,000 times 1000 equals 24 per thousand.
CDR equals 2,250 over 2,50,000 times 1000 equals 9 per thousand.
Natural growth rate equals CBR - CDR equals 24 minus 9 equals 15 per thousand 1.5 percent.
So the answer is CBR equals 24, CDR equals 9, growth equals 15 per thousand.
